paragraphs: In a wide-ranging interview broadcast from the White House on Newsmax’s "Finnerty" program, US President Donald Trump offered candid reflections on foreign diplomacy, strategic military planning, and international conflicts. The interview touched upon several pressing national security questions currently confronting Washington. When explicitly asked whether he trusts Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu just twelve days before Israel's upcoming parliamentary election on October 27, Trump declined to give a direct personal vote of confidence or endorse any candidate. Instead, he adopted a broad, cynical perspective on political life, declaring, "In the world of politics, I don't trust anyone." While acknowledging that various political figures in Israel would prefer him to actively intervene in Netanyahu’s campaign, Trump refrained from making any promises or offering an official political endorsement.

Despite his refusal to offer a firm personal endorsement, Trump praised the historical effectiveness of his working relationship with Netanyahu. He specifically highlighted the close military cooperation between the United States and Israel, crediting their past joint military operations with inflicting severe damage on the leadership and strategic capabilities of the Iranian regime. Displaying his characteristic bravado during the broadcast, Trump also boasted about his personal popularity among Israeli voters, claiming that he would easily secure ninety-nine percent of the vote if he were eligible to run for prime minister in Israel himself.

The conversation turned to escalating regional tensions following reports that the Pentagon had drafted fresh military strike options against Iran. According to media reports citing US officials, these Pentagon plans encompassed potential strikes against energy infrastructure and fortified nuclear facilities, including an underground site located beneath "Pickaxe Mountain." Military planners reportedly examined the potential deployment of the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast, widely known as the "Mother of All Bombs." Weighing approximately 9.8 tons, it is the largest non-nuclear weapon in the American military arsenal. Trump emphasized that the device is strictly conventional, comparing its immense destructive power to a small nuclear blast while explicitly ruling out atomic weapons or placing US ground troops in Iran.

Expanding on strategic defense matters, Trump asserted that the United States maintains the world's most formidable nuclear arsenal, positioned ahead of second-place Russia and third-place China, though he cautioned that Beijing could bridge the gap within five years. While advocating for global nuclear disarmament, he acknowledged the complex geopolitical challenges involved. Finally, Trump turned his attention to Eastern Europe, expressing sharp dissatisfaction with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Trump described Zelensky as a difficult leader who claims to desire a negotiated settlement while acting otherwise. He specifically criticized Ukrainian military strikes on Russian oil refineries, arguing that damaging diesel-producing facilities unnecessarily inflates global energy prices. Noting the intense personal hatred between Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin, Trump suggested that Ukraine should consider holding fresh presidential elections to break the diplomatic stalemate.

facts.fact: In an interview on Newsmax's 'Finnerty' show, Donald Trump declined to explicitly endorse Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of the October 27 Israeli elections, stating 'In the world of politics, I don't trust anyone.'

Trump noted that Israeli figures wanted him involved in Netanyahu's campaign, but he made no commitments, though he praised past military partnership with Israel against Iran and claimed he would get 99% of the vote if he ran in Israel.

Trump addressed reports regarding Pentagon attack plans on Iran, including targets at an underground nuclear site beneath Pickaxe Mountain and potential use of the 9.8-ton GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB).

Trump clarified that MOAB is a non-nuclear weapon with massive conventional power, explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons or deploying ground troops in Iran, and highlighted US nuclear superiority over Russia and China.

Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, criticizing Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries for driving up global fuel prices, citing mutual hatred between Putin and Zelensky, and suggesting Ukraine hold elections.
